newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Africa Israel boosts slow Israeli share market.
newsitem.headline: Africa Israel boosts slow Israeli share market.

text.p: A sharp increase in Africa Israel Investments helped push Israeli shares higher in what otherwise would have been a dull and probably weaker market, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.60 points, or 0.34 percent, to 174.98 on an all-share turnover of 57 million shekels unchanged from Monday.
The Maof 25 index gained 0.50 percent to 185.91.
"The market is simply not interesting any more. Despite the rise in Africa Israel nothing happens in it," said Ari Eidelhet at Zeler Eblagon Securities.

"The shekel is rising and this is bad for Israel exporters so there is no reason to believe that the negative trend will change in the near future. If it was not for Africa Israel the market would have closed lower also today," he said.

Africa Israel, the most active share, surged the maximum 10 percent to 426,797 on volume of 5.7 million shekels. The share rose following reports in Israeli press that entrepreneur Motti Zisser and industrialist Eitan Wertheimer raised credit of 250 million shekels to buy 18-20 percent of Africa Israel in order to raise their stake in the company to 25 percent. Such a stake will allow them to undermine the spin off of Migdal from Africa Israel, press reports said.
Traders said there were rumours that someone was trying to buy Africa shares for the value of $5 million at 15 percent above the market price.

Zisser and Wertheimer already hold a 6.82 percent stake in Africa Israel and last week they told local papers they had withdrawn their bid to purchase an Africa Israel stake from Bank Leumi because Leumi had decided to spin off Africa's insurance subsidiary, Migdal, from Africa before selling it off. Italian insurer Generali has offered to purchase Migdal.

IDB Holdings rose 3.75 percent to 1,090 on volume of 2.0 million shekels. Traders said that the share rose as investors predict that Wertheimer, along with his father Stef, might use the credit to buy shares in IDB. Wertheimer tried in the past to force the IDB group to sell its holding in tool maker, Iscar, which is owned by his family.

The Israel Corp plunged 5.75 percent to 19,073 after it reported net profit of 11.2 million shekels in the second quarter of 1996 as against net loss of 5.6 million shekels at the same quarter in 1995. During the first half of 1996 net profit rose to 49.1 million shekels from 372 thousand shekels in the first six months of 1995.

Clal Israel rose 0.5 percent to 6,751 after it said that net profit in the second quarter of 1996 fell to 44.6 million shekels from 58.9 million in the same quarter in 1995. During the first half of 1996 net profit was 107.7 million shekels as against 76.9 million shekels in the first six months of 1995.
"The market was really sleepy through most of the trading day. Only towards the end of the session activity rose a little," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.

Other active shares include Koor Industries which fell 1.25 percent to 27,234 on volume of 3.4 million shekels and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 0.25 percent to 113,476 on volume of 2.0 million shekels.
